en.g: Avoid false friends: words like actually, eventually, sensible and library.
p: Actually = in fact, really (not currently). Eventually = in the end, finally (not possibly).
Sensible = practical, reasonable (sensitive = easily upset). Library = place to borrow books (bookshop = buy).
Others: a career is a profession, not a race; to assist means to help, not to attend; a lecture is a talk.
en.q: Which false friends between English and your language have caught you out? Share a funny example.
en.c: Make a list of five false friends between English and your language, with the correct meaning of each.

de.g: Du vermeidest falsche Freunde wie actually, eventually, sensible und library.
p: Actually = eigentlich, tatsächlich (nicht aktuell). Eventually = schließlich, am Ende (nicht eventuell).
Sensible = vernünftig (sensibel = sensitive). Library = Bibliothek (Buchhandlung = bookshop).
Weitere: become = werden (nicht bekommen = get), gift = Geschenk, chef = Koch (nicht Chef = boss).

de.c: Notiere fünf falsche Freunde zwischen Deutsch und Englisch mit der richtigen Bedeutung.

es.g: Evita falsos amigos como actually, eventually, sensible y library.

Otros: embarrassed = avergonzado (no embarazada = pregnant), carpet = alfombra, assist = ayudar (no asistir = attend).

en.g: Grow your vocabulary through word families: create, creation, creative, creatively.
p: One root, many forms: create (verb), creation (noun), creative (adjective), creatively (adverb), creator (person).
Common endings: -tion, -ment, -ness for nouns; -ive, -ful, -able for adjectives; -ly for adverbs.
Prefixes change meaning: possible / impossible, agree / disagree, understand / misunderstand.

Typische Endungen: -tion, -ment, -ness für Nomen; -ive, -ful, -able für Adjektive; -ly für Adverbien.
Vorsilben ändern die Bedeutung: possible / impossible, agree / disagree, understand / misunderstand.

en.g: Use academic words for study and work: analyse, significant, approach, evidence, factor.
p: Analyse = examine in detail. Significant = important or large: a significant increase. Approach = a way of dealing with something.
Evidence is uncountable: There is evidence that... (not an evidence). Factor = one thing that influences a result.
More: assess, indicate, establish, consequently, a wide range of. They make writing precise and neutral.
en.q: What factors influence how well people learn a language? Use three academic words in your answer.
en.c: Rewrite this in academic style: Lots of people think the new rule is a big deal, and there's proof.

de.g: Du nutzt akademische Wörter für Studium und Beruf: analyse, significant, approach, evidence, factor.
p: Analyse = genau untersuchen. Significant = bedeutend: a significant increase. Approach = Herangehensweise.
Evidence ist unzählbar: There is evidence that... (nicht an evidence). Factor = ein Einflussfaktor.
Mehr: assess, indicate, establish, consequently, a wide range of. Sie machen Texte präzise und sachlich.

p: Analyse = examinar a fondo. Significant = importante o notable: a significant increase. Approach = enfoque.

en.g: Build compounds like time-consuming, well-known, bus stop and user-friendly.
p: Compound nouns: noun + noun, usually stress on the first part: a BUS stop, a TOOTHbrush, a phone charger.
Compound adjectives often use a hyphen before a noun: a well-known writer, a time-consuming task.
Numbers + noun stay singular: a ten-minute walk, a two-hour film. Other: user-friendly, eco-friendly.
en.q: Describe your town or job using three compound adjectives. Is anything there user-friendly or time-consuming?
en.c: Create six compounds: three nouns and three adjectives, and use each in a short sentence.

de.g: Du bildest Komposita wie time-consuming, well-known, bus stop und user-friendly.
p: Zusammengesetzte Nomen: Nomen + Nomen, Betonung meist vorn: a BUS stop, a TOOTHbrush, a phone charger.
Zusammengesetzte Adjektive vor einem Nomen meist mit Bindestrich: a well-known writer, a time-consuming task.
Zahl + Nomen bleibt Singular: a ten-minute walk, a two-hour film. Weitere: user-friendly, eco-friendly.
de.q: Beschreibe deine Stadt oder deinen Job mit drei zusammengesetzten Adjektiven. Ist etwas user-friendly oder time-consuming?

es.g: Forma compuestos como time-consuming, well-known, bus stop y user-friendly.

Los adjetivos compuestos llevan guion delante del sustantivo: a well-known writer, a time-consuming task.
Número + sustantivo va en singular: a ten-minute walk, a two-hour film. Otros: user-friendly, eco-friendly.

es.c: Crea seis compuestos, tres sustantivos y tres adjetivos, y usa cada uno en una frase corta.

fr.g: Forme des mots composés comme time-consuming, well-known, bus stop et user-friendly.
p: Noms composés : nom + nom, accent souvent sur le premier : a BUS stop, a TOOTHbrush, a phone charger.
Les adjectifs composés prennent un trait d'union devant un nom : a well-known writer, a time-consuming task.
Nombre + nom reste au singulier : a ten-minute walk, a two-hour film. Autres : user-friendly, eco-friendly.

en.g: Run a meeting smoothly with phrases like Let's get started, Moving on to and To sum up.
p: Open: Let's get started. Thanks for coming. The aim of today's meeting is to... We have three items on the agenda.
Manage: Moving on to the next point... Let's hear from Ana. Can we come back to that later? We're running short of time.
Close: To sum up, we agreed that... Action points: Tom will... by Friday. Thanks, everyone.
en.q: Have you ever led a meeting or a group discussion? What was easy and what was difficult?
en.c: Write a three-line script for opening, moving on and closing a short team meeting.

Abschließen: To sum up, we agreed that... Action points: Tom will... by Friday. Thanks, everyone.

de.c: Schreib ein Drei-Zeilen-Skript: Eröffnung, Überleitung und Abschluss eines kurzen Team-Meetings.

en.g: Use signposting phrases to guide your audience through a presentation.
p: Introduce: Today I'd like to talk about... First, I'll talk about..., then... and finally...
Move on: Let's now turn to... This brings me to my next point. As you can see on this slide...
Conclude: To conclude... The key takeaway is... Thank you for listening. Signposts help listeners follow you.
en.q: If you gave a five-minute presentation about your hobby, what would your three main points be?
en.c: Plan a mini presentation: write your opening, two signposts and a closing sentence.

en.g: Respond to questions with confidence: That's a great question, Let me come back to that.

en.g: Make offers, concessions and counter-offers: We could agree to that on condition that...
p: Offer: We could offer... How about if we...? Counter-offer: That's a little high for us. Would you consider...?
Conditions: We could agree to that on condition that... / provided that / as long as you... Unless..., we can't...
Concede and close: I think we can meet you halfway. Let's shake on it. So, to confirm, we've agreed...
en.q: Have you ever negotiated something, like a price, a salary or a holiday plan? How did it go?
en.c: Role-play buying a used bike with your Buddy: make an offer, a counter-offer and agree with a condition.

en.g: Give feedback diplomatically: positive first, then suggestions like One thing you might consider is...
p: Start positive and specific: I really liked how you... Your introduction was very clear.
Suggest, don't command: One thing you might consider is... It might be worth... Have you thought about...?
Soften: slightly, a bit, perhaps. Not It's bad, but It could be a little shorter. End with encouragement.
en.q: How do you prefer to receive feedback: direct or diplomatic? Why?
en.c: Write diplomatic feedback for a friend's imaginary presentation: one strength, two suggestions, one encouragement.

Abschwächen: slightly, a bit, perhaps. Nicht It's bad, sondern It could be a little shorter. Mit Ermutigung enden.
